title: PR throughput drift ensemble detector and synthetic shadowing for CI gating
creator: Nina Patel
description: Add an ensemble-based performance drift detector to PR CI that combines statistical changepoint detection, EWMA smoothing, and bootstrap baselines; complement this with a small synthetic shadowing harness that replays representative token streams for affected models so we can compute stable tokens/sec and p95 estimates at PR time. Goal: reduce noisy false positives from single-run comparisons and improve signal quality for gating decisions.
acceptance_criteria: CI check (GitHub Action) runs for any PR that touches runtime or scheduler code and produces a numeric 'drift_score' artifact
Drift score algorithm uses at least two independent signals (Bayesian changepoint on time series + bootstrap delta on median tokens/sec) and yields a single normalized 0..1 score

Synthetic shadowing harness replays model-specific token distributions (short/medium/long sequences) in <= 10 minutes using a lightweight replica job and returns p50/p95 tokens/sec and memory footprint
Default gating policy: block PR if drift_score >= 0.9 AND relative p95 degradation >= 7% with p-value <= 0.01; otherwise post a warning comment with links to traces
Historical backtest shows false positive rate <= 2% on last 12 months of PRs used in our dataset
Results posted to PR as a check with a link to a per-PR dashboard snapshot and a reproducible job spec
Unit tests for detector components and an integration smoke test in the CI matrix
implementation_notes: Pipeline components: (1) lightweight runner to produce synthetic load, (2) time-series ingestion of last N baseline runs, (3) ensemble detector service that computes drift_score, (4) GH Action that coordinates jobs and comments

Baseline construction: keep rolling bootstrap of the last 30 successful CI baseline runs per model+config; preserve environment fingerprint (CUDA, driver, kernel) and only compare to baselines with matching fingerprint when available

Detector design: use Bayesian online changepoint detection for abrupt breaks + EWMA with adaptive alpha to capture gradual drift. Final drift_score = weighted sigmoid of normalized changepoint confidence and bootstrap effect size. Weights configurable per project.
Stat testing: use bootstrap resampling to compute p-values for p95 change; use percentile bootstrap because distributions are heavy-tailed for p95
Resource controls: synthetic shadow jobs use a job spec that limits concurrency and tokens to keep cost < 0.2 credits per PR in expected median case
Fallback: if synthetic shadow can't run (quota/timeouts), fall back to an embargoed 'soft warning' that does not block PR, but records the gap for telemetry
test_plan: Unit tests for EWMA and Bayesian changepoint modules with deterministic seeds
Simulated PR replay: run detector on a held-out set of historical PRs (n=120) and confirm drift_score aligns with known regressions and benign changes
A/B validation: enable detector on a subset of repos as non-blocking warnings for 2 weeks and compare actionable noise rate vs current heuristics
End-to-end CI dry-run: create GH Action that checks out PR, runs synthetic shadow on a small GPU runner, collects tokens/sec/p95, runs detector, and posts check output
Load safety: run synthetic shadow harness against a staging cluster during off-hours and verify autoscaling does not trigger unexpectedly
comments: 2026-02-12 Nina Patel: Initial spike of design ideas after sync with Runtime team. Decided to prefer ensemble over single-statistic gates to reduce flakiness.
2026-02-19 Marco Alvarez: Prototyped EWMA + bootstrap in pybench harness. Early results show many ~3% fluctuations that would be false positives with existing thresholds.
2026-02-27 QA: Need deterministic seeding for p95 bootstrap to make unit tests reliable. Also flagged that driver mismatch skews p95 on identical codepaths.
2026-03-03 Product: Suggest PR comment include guidance text and link to a 'how to diagnose' doc for engs to iterate on performance regressions quickly.

2026-03-11 Marco Alvarez: Added adaptive fingerprint matching; now we check CUDA/driver/kernel strings and fall back to nearest-neighbor baseline if exact match not found (recorded as heuristic in metadata).
